10.1002/adfm.77583.abstract: In this work, a nitro-functionalized PDOL gel polymer electrolyte was developed for lithium–sulfur batteries through the in situ copolymerization of DOL with R-glycidyl nosylate. This molecular design reconstructs the Li + coordination environment and establishes a multidimensional dynamic transport network, thereby promoting fast Li + migration and stable interfacial chemistry. Meanwhile, the electrolyte induces the in situ formation of a fluorine-/nitrogen-rich gradient SEI, effectively suppressing lithium dendrite growth, and polysulfide shuttle. As a result, the PDOL@R-GN electrolyte enables high-performance lithium–sulfur batteries under practical operating conditions. ABSTRACT Rational design of lithium-ion coordination architectures within gel polymer electrolytes remains challenging for simultaneously improving ionic transport and interfacial stability in lithium-sulfur batteries. Herein, we report an in situ copolymerization strategy of 1,3-dioxolane (DOL) with π -conjugated nitroaromatic R-glycidyl nosylate (R-GN). The π -conjugated structure promotes electron-density delocalization onto the nitro group, reducing N═O bond polarity compared with conventional nitrate additives. The resulting PDOL@R-GN electrolyte builds a multidimensional lithium-ion coordination network through electronic modulation and spatial effects, enabling preferential Li + transport and a high Li + transference number (tLi+${{{{t}}}_{{\mathrm{L}}{{{\mathrm{i}}}^ + }}}$ = 0.66) at 25°C. It also promotes a gradient solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) with F- and N-rich components, improving interfacial robustness and ionic transport. Pouch-cell feasibility was demonstrated using a 3 Ah pouch cell, delivering 392 Wh kg −1 under high sulfur loading (8 mg cm −2 ), and lean electrolyte (E/S = 3 g electrolyt e g s −1 ), while retaining 811 mAh g −1 after 40 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 95.0%. This work provides insights into the molecular-level design of multifunctional electrolytes for high-energy-density batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78097.abstract: Interlayer Cu─N coordination chains in pyrimidinyl-grafted COFs bridge stacked layers into electronically cooperative channels, synchronizing ordered porosity with cross-plane charge transport to enable efficient, selective nitrate-to-ammonia electrocatalysis under neutral conditions. ABSTRACT Efficient multielectron electrocatalysis in layered covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is frequently limited by weak cross-plane charge delivery to pore-confined active sites. Herein, we report the construction of two metal-bridged COFs (Py1-COF-Cu and Py2-COF-Cu) by incorporating nitrogen-containing heterocycles to facilitate interlayer Cu─N coordination. This design generates continuous linear coordination chains within the 1D channels while maintaining high intrinsic porosity. Synchrotron XANES confirms the Cu─N coordination environment, and DFT reveals realigned frontier-orbital energetics together with pronounced redistribution of electron density along the interlayer direction. Among them, the optimized Py2-COF-Cu serves as a highly active cathode catalyst for the electroreduction of nitrate to ammonia in neutral media. It delivers a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 87.8% and a peak NH 3 yield rate of 4964.6 µmol h −1 mg −1 at -1.0 V vs. RHE, comparable to leading Cu-based NO 3 RR catalysts. This interlayer coordination motif provides a structural lever to couple ordered porosity with effective cross-plane charge transport for demanding multielectron reactions.

10.1002/adfm.78151.abstract: A Cu–Ti heterometallic MOF is developed as a high-performance catalyst for selective methylamine synthesis from co-electrolysis of CO 2 and NO 3 − . Using an integrated reaction system achieves an unprecedented Faradaic efficiency of 86.28% and methylamine yield rate of 132.02 mmol h −1 g −1 . ABSTRACT Electrochemical C-N coupling offers a sustainable pathway for organonitrogen synthesis but faces kinetic challenges in reactant activation and C-N coupling for target product generation. Herein, we report a heterometallic metal-organic framework (MOF), Cu-MIL-125, as a high-performance catalyst for selective methylamine synthesis from co-electrolysis of CO 2 and NO 3 − . In situ spectroscopic experiments and theoretical calculations unravel that the constructed heterometallic Cu–Ti sites on Cu-MIL-125 synergistically promote key * HCHO/ * NH 2 OH intermediate generation and boost their C-N coupling and hydrogenation energetics, while simultaneously facilitating reactant accumulation and side reaction suppression. Moreover, by integrating plasma-assisted nitrogen fixation, cathodic methylamine electrosynthesis coupled with anodic glycerol oxidation in a zero-gap MEA electrolyzer, we achieve an unprecedented Faradaic efficiency of 86.28% with a methylamine yield rate of 132.02 mmol h −1 g −1 , representing one of the best performances thus far. Our strategy establishes a scalable, economically viable, and carbon-neutral paradigm for the decentralized synthesis of organonitrogen chemicals.

10.1002/adfm.78179.abstract: Nitro-functionalized nucleophilic molecular design endows DNIQ with highly delocalized redox-active sites for rapid NH 4 + capture. The resulting CDI system delivers record-level removal capacity, efficient energy recovery, and scalable wastewater treatment potential. ABSTRACT The increasing discharge of ammonium-rich wastewater has become a critical challenge for aquatic ecosystems and sustainable nitrogen management, creating an urgent need for efficient NH 4 + removal and recovery technologies. Among emerging electrochemical approaches, capacitive deionization (CDI) is attractive because of its low energy consumption and mild operating conditions, yet its practical performance is still largely limited by electrode materials. In this study, we developed a nitro-functionalized organic electrode based on dinitro-isoquinoxaline (DNIQ), featuring a rigid fused-ring π-conjugated framework and well-defined redox-active sites. The introduced nitro groups markedly lower the LUMO energy level and redistribute electron density within the conjugated framework, while enhancing the interaction of the C═N and NO 2 sites with NH 4 + . Experimental results show that the DNIQ electrode retains 81.84% of its capacity after 6000 cycles. When assembled into a CDI system, it delivers a record NH 4 + removal capacity of 273.89 mg g −1 and an ultrafast removal rate of 42.39 mg g −1 min −1 at 1.4 V, while maintaining 100% capacity retention over 100 cycles. This work provides a molecular-level strategy for efficient ammonium capture and sustainable nitrogen recovery.

10.1002/adfm.78323.abstract: By enhancing the effective spin–orbit coupling (SOC) of active sites through B-induced Pd–B orbital hybridization, PdCuB nanosheets overcome the spin-forbidden kinetic limitation of *NO coupling during NO 3 RR, thereby enabling highly selective and durable electrocatalytic nitrate-to-N 2 conversion. ABSTRACT The selectivity bottleneck of electrochemical nitrate-to-N 2 conversion is kinetic rather than thermodynamic: dimerization of two adsorbed *NO intermediates is spin-forbidden, imposing a kinetic barrier invisible to conventional thermodynamic analyses. Spin–orbit coupling (SOC) offers the principal channel for the required spin-state crossing, yet its deliberate use as a design variable in nitrate reduction remains unexplored. Here we show that covalent Pd─B bonding in ultrathin PdCuB alloy nanosheets breaks the local coordination symmetry at Pd sites, partially lifts the crystal-field quenching of orbital angular momentum, and enhances the effective SOC without toxic heavy-metal dopants. Electron paramagnetic resonance reveals a two-stage evolution of the g-factor with B content, converging at g = 1.910 for the optimal composition. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory indicate that, although *NO dimerization is thermodynamically favorable, its spin-forbidden character dominates selectivity, and the B-induced electronic and SOC-related perturbation facilitates intersystem crossing, rendering the N 2 pathway kinetically accessible. The optimized nanosheets deliver 83% N 2 Faradaic efficiency at +0.11 V versus RHE with over 1100 h stability, establishing light p-block element incorporation as a heavy-metal-free strategy to address spin-forbidden bond-forming steps in nitrogen electrocatalysis.

10.1002/adfm.79042.abstract: ABSTRACT The regeneration of graphite anodes from spent lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for sustainable battery recycling. Existing strategies typically rely on energy‐intensive graphitization or hazardous chemical treatments, which are either ineffective in repairing intrinsic defects or environmentally unsustainable. Here, we show that spent graphite largely retains its graphitic framework and therefore requires selective healing of localized defects and removal of surface residues, rather than complete structural reconstruction. We develop an ultrafast thermal strategy using flash Joule heating (2273 K within 0.1 s, held for 10 s), which simultaneously repairs lattice defects and removes surface residues with minimal thermal budget. Moreover, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are integrated into graphite and ultrafast thermal treatment enables interfacial fusion between CNTs and graphite domains, reconstructing long‐range conductive pathways across particles. This process transforms CNTs from passive conductive additives into active structural reconstruction agents. As a result, the regenerated graphite exhibits enhanced structural integrity and electron transport, delivering superior rate capability, cycling stability, and low‐temperature performance. In addition, the process suppresses thermal‐shock‐induced powder loss and significantly reduces energy consumption. This work establishes a mechanism‐driven strategy for defect‐selective healing and conductive‐network reconstruction in spent graphite, providing a promising and sustainable pathway for lithium‐ion battery recycling.

10.1002/adfm.79331.abstract: A facile supramolecular self-assembly strategy of 4-sulfocalix[6]arene (SCA[6]) and N,N’-dimethyl-9,9’-biacridinium dinitrate (LCG), driven by cooperative host–guest recognition and electrostatic interactions, creates a protective interphase on Zn anodes. Acting as a “molecular switch”, this interphase modulates Zn 2 + solvation, accelerates ion transport, and alleviates cycling-induced volume fluctuations, yielding stable supramolecular protective multilayers for prolonged cycling lifespan. ABSTRACT The instability of zinc anodes during reversible deposition and dissolution in the aqueous electrolyte constitutes a critical bottleneck limiting the lifespan of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Herein, we utilize a straightforward and supramolecular self-assembly approach involving 4-sulfocalix[6]arene (SCA[6]) and N,N’-dimethyl-9,9’-biacridinium dinitrate (LCG), driven by cooperative host-guest recognition and electrostatic forces. The spontaneous interfacial assembly of these components enables the construction of a protective interphase on zinc anodes and functions as a “molecular switch” to regulate the Zn 2 + solvation structure, facilitate ion transport, and accommodate volumetric fluctuations during cycling. Consequently, the LCG/SCA[6]-modified interface effectively mitigates corrosion and dendrite growth, thereby significantly enhancing the electrochemical stability and cycling performance of AZIBs. As a result, the (LCG/SCA[6]) 2 -Zn symmetric cell can maintain stable operation for over 3800 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . The (LCG/SCA[6]) 2 -Zn||I 2 coin cell retains a specific capacity of 200.50 mAh g −1 with a capacity retention rate of 87.25% at 2 A g −1 even after 14 000 cycles. Considering the low cost and simplicity of LCG/SCA[6] film fabrication, this supramolecular composite presents a promising strategy for enhancing the stability of zinc anodes.

10.1002/adfm.79368.abstract: Atomically dispersed Ag sites on MoS 2 create a favorable reaction environment for the electroreduction of nitrates. These sites enhance nitrate adsorption, stabilize NOx-derived intermediates, and direct active hydrogen to subsequent hydrogenation reactions rather than hydrogen evolution reactions. Ag-MoS 2 nanosheet aggregates achieve high ammonia selectivity, ampere-level current density, a yield of 30.6 mg h −1 cm −2 , and stable operation for up to 200 h. ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR) to ammonia (NH 3 ) offers a sustainable route for coupling nitrate (NO 3 − ) remediation with NH 3 synthesis. However, its efficiency is often limited by the insufficient NO 3 − activation, incomplete hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates, and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we report a catalyst consisting of Ag single atoms anchored on flower-like MoS 2 nanosheet aggregates (Ag-MoS 2 NAs) for efficient NO 3 − -to-NH 3 conversion. Ag-MoS 2 NAs feature a high loading of isolated Ag sites while preserving atomic dispersion, providing abundant NO 3 − activation centers. During NO 3 − -to-NH 3 conversion, Ag sites promote NO 3 − adsorption and initial deoxygenation steps, whereas MoS 2 provides active hydrogen species for the subsequent hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates. The integration of these complementary functions enables efficient NO 3 − activation and subsequent hydrogenation, thereby enhancing NH 3 production and achieving a Faradaic efficiency of up to 95%. As a result, the Ag-MoS 2 NAs maintain stable operation for over 200 h at current densities exceeding 400 mA cm −2 , achieving an NH 3 yield rate of 30.6 mg h −1 cm −2 . This work demonstrates that integrating NO 3 − activation sites with hydrogenation functionalities in a single catalyst can effectively promote NH 3 production from NO 3 − under industrially relevant conditions.

10.1002/adfm.79376.abstract: This work provides a comprehensive understanding of reconstruction-induced interfacial coupling chemistry. By correlating catalyst reconstruction, interfacial chemistry, ion transport, and mechanical coupling, we demonstrate how electrochemical reconstruction can simultaneously regulate catalytic activity and electrode/electrolyte interfaces, offering new guidance for the rational design of durable gel electrochemical energy storage devices. ABSTRACT Gel zinc-air batteries (GZABs) are promising for flexible energy storage. However, their performance is often limited by unstable gel cathode interfaces, where water-dependent OH − transport, charge transfer, and mechanical adhesion are closely linked. Here, we propose an interfacial coupling chemistry by using a cobalt-based Prussian blue analogue (CCN) as a reconstructable precatalyst. When assembled with a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) gel electrolyte and electrochemically activated during the GZAB operation, CCN was reconstructed into a sheet-arrayed amorphous CoOOH while releasing cyanide-derived nitrogen that was confined by the gel network and converted into −NO 2 groups at the PVA/CoOOH interface. These NO 2 groups act as molecular linkers, chemically coupling with CoOOH through Co–N–O bonding and reinforcing hydrogen bonding with the PVA chains. The in situ reconstructed electrode exhibits enhanced interfacial OH − transport, with an apparent diffusion coefficient 3.25 times that of the ex situ construction, together with lower interfacial resistance and stronger mechanical adhesion. Benefiting from both the reconstructed CoOOH catalyst and coupling interface, the resulting GZAB delivers a peak power density of 144 mW cm −2 and maintains 86.4 mW cm −2 even at 30% water content. The enhanced interfacial adhesion further enables stable operation in omnidirectionally flexible cable-type zinc-air batteries.

10.1002/adma.74297.abstract: Near-critical thinning turns porous polyethylene from a hydrophobic, electrically insulating barrier into a thickness-gated membrane electrode. As the membrane approaches ∼60 nm, blocked mass and electron transport become accessible without changing chemistry, enabling hydrophobic-yet-permeable, electronically addressable polymer interfaces for liquid-phase electrochemical conversion. ABSTRACT Electrochemical systems are constrained by a materials paradox: chemically robust porous separators are typically hydrophobic and electronically insulating, forcing bulky, carbon-rich interfaces to couple mass transport and electrical contact. Here we show that pushing freestanding porous polyethylene into a near-critical ultrathin regime turns thickness into a geometric gate, enabling these functions to be switched without chemical modification. Near an inferred lower bound (∼10 nm), a 60 nm membrane already enters this regime: liquid-entry pressure collapses into a sub-bar window, enabling aqueous-electrolyte permeation, while the electrical threshold shifts to sub-volt soft dielectric breakdown, yielding persistent through-plane conductivity. The same scaffold enhances nanowire-matrix coupling via high conformability and real contact area, enabling a binder- and carbon-free ∼300 nm ultrathin membrane electrode. As a stringent liquid-phase electrochemical validation, this membrane electrode drives selective nitrate-to-ammonia electroreduction in flowing alkaline electrolytes with sustained performance. Near-critical ultrathinness thus emerges as a gateable design dimension for re-imagining commodity plastics as transmembrane-active platforms.

10.1002/adma.74572.abstract: Thermal nitrate decomposition drives an inside-out multiscale reconstruction of Ni-rich cathodes. By integrating a stress-buffering central pore, a strain-retardant perovskite phase, and a protective surface layer, this architecture synchronizes chemomechanical stabilization and Li + transport. The resulting cathode suppresses oxygen evolution and microcracking, delivering outstanding stability and rate capability under high-voltage and elevated-temperature conditions. ABSTRACT Ni-rich layered oxides (LiNi x Co y Mn 1− x − y O 2 , x ≥ 0.8) are indispensable for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries, yet they suffer from severe chemomechanical degradation driven by the synergy of internal microcracking and interfacial parasitic side reactions. Existing strategies inherently suffer from decoupled regulation of mechanical and chemical instabilities that fail to address these issues holistically. Here, we develop an inside-out structural reconfiguration strategy driven by the thermal decomposition of nitrates, concurrently tailoring the core, bulk, and surface of NCM811 in a single calcination step. This reconstruction generates a stress-buffering central pore architecture that effectively homogenizes anisotropic lattice strain and suppresses crack nucleation. Concurrently, the regulated Nd 3+ diffusion forms a coherent Nd 4 [LiNi]O 8 (NLNO) perovskite phase within the bulk lattice, creating a pinning effect that stabilizes the layered framework and enhances charge transport. Furthermore, excess Nd-species evolve into a conformal NLNO surface coating, acting as a physical barrier and oxygen reservoir to resist electrolyte attack and oxygen evolution. The modified cathode delivers an exceptional capacity retention (95.7% after 200 cycles at 4.5 V) and exceptional rate capability (157.1 mAh g −1 at 5 C). Even under stringent conditions (4.6 V or 45°C), a superior retention of 87.8% is maintained after 200 cycles, demonstrating remarkable chemomechanical robustness.

10.1002/adma.74714.abstract: This work proposes a cross-scale strategy to construct Cu/MoS 2 nanoreactor consisting of hollow MoS 2 loaded with Cu single atoms and clusters. Its heat-exchanger-fin-like structure and dual-species spillover effect break mass-transfer and energy-barrier bottlenecks for boosted nitrate-to-ammonia reduction. In real wastewater, the assembled Al-NO 3 − battery achieves stable power generation, efficient nitrate removal, and ammonia electrosynthesis. ABSTRACT Copper-based materials are promising catalysts for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia (NH 3 ), while their use in real wastewater with low nitrate concentrations is hindered by poor mass transfer and high energy barrier. To overcome these limitations, we design a hollow Cu/MoS 2 -550 nanoreactor, consisting of hollow MoS 2 support loaded with Cu single atoms and clusters. At the mesoscale, the hollow MoS 2 support features a heat-exchanger-fin-like structure that accelerates mass transfer, thereby promoting local enrichment of NO 3 − . At the microscale, precise modulation of sulfur vacancy concentration in MoS 2 triggers dual-species spillover, namely reverse hydrogen spillover and *NO spillover from Cu single atoms to Cu clusters, which lowers the energy barrier of deep hydrogenation step. As a result, the Cu/MoS 2 -550 nanoreactor achieves an NH 3 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 98.14% and a yield rate of 27.46 mg h −1 mg cat −1 . Furthermore, when assembled into an Al-NO 3 − battery operating in real wastewater containing only ∼ 0.76 mM NO 3 − , the battery runs stably for 120 h, delivers an NH 3 FE of 53.20%, and maintains a nitrate removal rate of 91.17%. This work provides cross-scale modulation strategies to overcome mass-transfer bottlenecks and energy barriers in multi-electron transfer reactions, offering a potential pathway for environmental applications.

10.1002/adma.74915.abstract: In this study, we have synthesized unconventional face-centered cubic (fcc) RuW alloy nanoflowers, which exhibit excellent NH 3 Faradaic efficiency (FE) above 91.0% over a wide pH range from 1 to 14. Importantly, fcc RuW nanoflowers adaptively steer reaction pathways toward diverse pH environments. These fcc RuW nanoflowers also demonstrate excellent catalytic stability at an industrial-level current density of 300 mA cm −2 . ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) to ammonia has been regarded as a sustainable strategy for industrial wastewater denitrification and fertilizer manufacturing toward green nitrogen circulation. However, complex pH conditions of practical nitrate wastewater result in poor catalyst universality, severely hindering their long-term deployment. Furthermore, the underlying reaction mechanisms in different pH scenarios remain ambiguous, obstructing the rational design of pH-universal electrocatalysts. Here we propose a crystal phase engineering approach to enhance the NO 3 RR performance in complex pH scenarios. The as-designed unconventional face-centered cubic (fcc) RuW nanoflowers exhibit excellent ammonia Faradaic efficiency (FE) above 91.0% over a wide pH range of 1–14, with the largest yield rate of 40.1 mg h −1 mg cat −1 . Mechanism studies indicate that fcc RuW nanoflowers adaptively steer reaction pathways toward diverse pH environments. Based on the long-term durability test at an industrial-level current density of 300 mA cm −2 for 200 h in flow reactors, techno-economic analysis with the optimized process further demonstrates promising application potential. This study not only provides a fundamental insight into the pH-dependent mechanisms of nitrate electroreduction, but also offers a robust catalyst design approach toward complex practical conditions.

10.1002/adma.74943.abstract: A p-type tetraazanaphthotetraphene ligand enables precise control over single-atom Ni sites in a hollow conductive MOF, accelerating proton transfer and hydrogenation kinetics for electrocatalytic NO reduction. This strategy delivers exceptional ammonia production and enables a Zn-NO battery with 2.1 mW cm −2 power density. ABSTRACT Electrochemical reduction of ammonia represents a highly promising approach for transforming harmful environmental pollutants into more valuable products. In this study, we successfully achieved precise control over the environment surrounding single-atom Ni sites by modifying functional groups on ligands. To validate this strategy, we constructed two similar hollow Ni-MOFs. The metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) containing the p-type tetraazanaphthotetraphene ligand (Ni-TT) demonstrated exceptional performance compared to n-type triphenylene (Ni-TP). Its overall reduction rate reached 196.9 µmol·h −1 ·cm 2 , with a Faraday efficiency as high as 90.9% at −0.4 V versus RHE. The exceptional performance of Ni-TT stems from the p-type tetranaphthalenetetracene ligand, which is nitrogen-rich and electron-deficient. The electronic properties of the ligand significantly influence the coordination environment around the single-atom Ni site, enabling precise control over proton-transfer behavior during the reaction. Theoretical calculations also indicate that hydrogen adsorption on p-type Ni-TT surfaces accelerates hydrogen transfer at Ni active sites compared to n-type Ni-TP. This significantly enhances the rate-determining step (RDS) in the NO hydrogenation process. The constructed Ni-TT-based Zn-NO battery achieved a power density of 2.1 mW cm −2 . These results provide insight into how conjugated ligand structures modulate the electronic structure and hydrogenation behavior, which may guide future studies on MOF-based electrocatalysts for nitric oxide reduction reaction (NORR).

10.1002/adma.75456.abstract: Metal–organic framework-derived Co 3 O 4 (MD-Co 3 O 4 ) features oxygen-vacancies that selectively reconstruct octahedral cobalt (CoOh) sites into an electron-rich, high-spin state. The resulting CoOh centers strengthen nitrate adsorption and accelerate its conversion to ammonia, delivering a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% along with superior stability and broad applicability. ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon-free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber–Bosch process is energy-intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. Herein, we report a metal–organic framework (MOF)-derived Co 3 O 4 electrocatalyst (MD-Co 3 O 4 ) prepared by controlled pyrolysis of Co-MOF-74, which achieved a high Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% and excellent stability for the electrosynthesis of NH 3 from nitrate, along with robust activity over a wide pH and nitrate concentration range. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the oxygen vacancies generated during MOF pyrolysis induce coordination distortion of octahedral Co sites, leading to a high-spin state transition with an electron-rich configuration that synergistically enhances nitrate adsorption and interfacial electron transfer, thereby boosting the intrinsic activity. Moreover, this MOF-based strategy is applicable to other M 1 Co 2 O 4 spinels, which provides an effective approach for spin engineering at the atomic scale and sustainable ammonia synthesis.

10.1002/adma.75462.abstract: A Co/Co 7 Fe 3 heterostructure is designed to drive electrocatalytic nitrate reduction via a unique [4+4] tandem mechanism. The interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerates water dissociation, and enables hydrogen spillover. Its heterointerfaces optimize the adsorption energetics of key intermediates, and its synergistic dual spillover enhances the reaction, delivering a high NH 3 yield rate with nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency. ABSTRACT Rational design of dual-site catalysts to decouple complex multi-electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co 7 Fe 3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO 3 RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4-electron step reduces NO 3 − to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4-electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4-electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well-defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co 7 Fe 3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO 3 RR through synergistic dual-spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near-unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH 3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h −1 cm −2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn-nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm −2 with excellent cycling stability. Solar‐driven gas‐phase N 2 /H 2 conversion requires catalysts that couple efficient light utilization with structural stability under H 2 ‐rich conditions. Accordingly, 5 wt% Ru/Nb‐CeO 2 achieves an NH 3 synthesis rate of 7.4 mmol g −1 h −1 at 350°C and 0.1 MPa and remains stable for 144 h. Kinetic analyses and in situ DRIFTS indicate that the electronically promoted Ru state alleviates N 2 ‐activation limitations and facilitates subsequent *NH x hydrogenation and NH 3 desorption. A screening‐level analysis estimates a catalyst‐and‐feedstock cost of 286–322 USD t NH3 −1 under the lower‐bound electricity scenario, 42%–51% below the selected Cs‐Ru/MgO benchmark within the same framework. These results identify lattice strain as a promising strategy for simultaneously stabilizing the oxygen sublattice and electronically promoting Ru for efficient solar‐driven ammonia synthesis.

10.1002/admi.70704.abstract: ABSTRACT 2D transition‐metal carbides and nitrides, known as MXenes, have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for nitrogen‐related reactions, including ammonia oxidation (AOR), nitrogen reduction (NRR), and nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR). Their appeal stems from a layered architecture, abundant active sites, tunable surface chemistry, and high electrical conductivity. Key physicochemical properties—including controllable surface terminations (–O, –OH, –F), defect‐rich surfaces, and flexible electronic structures—facilitate intermediate adsorption and activation while enhancing charge‐transfer kinetics. Recent synthesis methods, such as HF etching and fluorine‐free Lewis acid approaches, enable precise control over functionalities that dictate catalytic performance. Furthermore, engineering strategies like heteroatom doping, defect engineering, and hybrid composite formation are explored to optimize activity, selectivity, and durability. Ti 3 C 2 T X remains the most extensively studied platform due to its versatility and performance. This review provides a comprehensive overview of advancements in MXene‐based catalysts for NO 3 RR, NRR, and AOR, highlighting the relationships between reaction mechanisms, electronic structures, and synthesis strategies. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives for the rational design of efficient, scalable, and sustainable MXene catalysts for nitrogen‐related energy applications are discussed.

10.1002/adsu.70676.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic nitrate reduction is assessed through nitrate conversion, although the reaction can redistribute nitrogen among nitrite, nitric oxide (NO)‐derived intermediates, nitrous oxide (N 2 O), dinitrogen (N 2 ), ammonia/ammonium (NH 3 /NH 4 + ), and emerging C–N products. The environmental and resource value of the process depends on nitrogen fate rather than nitrate disappearance alone. This review establishes a product‐centred framework for understanding and steering that fate. We first consolidate the nitrogen network across surface, liquid, and gas phases, and distinguish primary selectivity from the final product distribution after secondary conversion and phase transfer. We then relate product formation to three coupled levels: nitrate entry, branching of NO‐derived intermediates, and branch completion; surface functions governing adsorption, intermediate binding, cooperative sites, and active hydrogen; and the photochemical redox environment, including charge delivery and the oxidation half‐reaction. Evidence from model systems, real waters, and time‐resolved operation shows why high selectivity under one condition cannot be treated as an intrinsic catalyst property. On this basis, N 2 ‐oriented treatment requires verified removal without nitrite, ammonium, or N 2 O leakage, whereas NH 3 ‐oriented conversion requires product preservation, capture, and a favourable process balance. Connecting working‐interface chemistry with water‐matrix effects, reactor operation, and product recovery provides a route from empirical nitrate removal to deliberate nitrogen management.

10.1002/advs.78256.abstract: ABSTRACT Utilizing NH 3 as a H 2 carrier has been proposed to address the storage and transportation bottlenecks of the green hydrogen supply chain. NH 3 thermal cracking is a conventional technique for H 2 recovery after transport, but its infrastructure‐intensive nature limits its application in decentralized H 2 production scenarios. Consequently, ammonia electrolysis, coined “e‐cracking” in this article, is proposed as a complementary technique for such scenarios. This emerging technique couples hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) with ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR), which was previously studied in the context of ammonia fuel cells. While thermal cracking has been extensively investigated regarding catalyst development and economic feasibility, e‐cracking is at an early stage and lacks such efforts, as reflected by its lower technology readiness level (TRL). To bridge this gap, this Perspective provides a comprehensive analysis of e‐cracking addressing both aspects. We begin with an overview of catalyst development for both techniques and then conduct a techno‐economic analysis (TEA) based on reported performance data. By comparing the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH), we demonstrate e‐cracking's theoretical potential for lower costs and identify the current limitations arising from catalytic performance. Finally, we provide an outlook on research directions and strategies to advance NH 3 e‐cracking toward practical implementation.

10.1002/aenm.71507.abstract: This work presents open AgRh alloy hollow nanocubes that turn nitrate pollutants into ammonia with high efficiency and stability. The catalyst uses cooperative silver and rhodium sites to activate nitrate and complete hydrogenation, while its porous hollow structure improves transport. It also enables a low-voltage nitrate reduction–hydrazine oxidation electrolyzer for energy-saving nitrogen conversion. ABSTRACT Electrochemical nitrate-to-ammonia (NO 3 − to NH 3 ) conversion offers a promising route for NO 3 − removal and distributed NH 3 synthesis. However, its efficiency is constrained by sluggish NO 3 − activation, incomplete hydrogenation, and competing hydrogen evolution. Herein, open AgRh alloy hollow nanocubes (AgRh hNCs) are reconstructed from Ag nanocubes through a chloride-assisted alloying and etching process. The catalyst possesses a porous, nanograin-assembled framework with a Rh-enriched near-surface region, enhancing both mass transport and interfacial electronic coupling. Consequently, AgRh hNCs achieve up to 98% Faradaic efficiency for NH 3 , an NH 3 yield rate of 10.6 mg h −1 mg cat −1 , and excellent durability in the alkaline nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Combined theoretical and experimental studies reveal a tandem-like interfacial step-matching mechanism, in which Ag promotes the NO 3 -to-NO 2 step, while Rh-centered sites drive deep hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates to NH 3 . Moreover, AgRh hNCs show high hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) activity, enabling a membrane-separated NO 3 RR||HzOR electrolyzer with a 1.58 V lower cell voltage than the oxygen evolution reaction-coupled system at 10 mA cm −2 . This work demonstrates that integrating an open hollow structure with cooperative Ag-Rh interfacial sites is an effective strategy for selective NO 3 − -to-NH 3 electrosynthesis.

10.1002/aenm.71587.abstract: CuBi 2 O 4 undergoes in situ electroreduction to reconstruct Cu─Bi interfacial sites for co-reduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − in urea electrosynthesis. The superior performance stems from * NO-promoted * CO adsorption and converting endergonic C─N coupling into exergonic N─C─N coupling. This work highlights a generalizable interfacial-site strategy for modulating reaction pathways in electrosynthetic C─N coupling systems. ABSTRACT Electrochemical urea synthesis via co-reduction of CO 2 and nitrate (NO 3 − ) offers a sustainable route for C─N bond formation but remains challenged by poor selectivity and competing side reactions. Here, we report a dual-metal interfacial engineering strategy that enables C─N coupling by favoring a key NO─M 1 ─NO─CO─M 2 configuration. Using CuBi 2 O 4 as a model precursor, in situ electroreduction induces reconstruction into an electron-enriched and low-coordinated Cu─Bi interfacial structure. Operando Raman and surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy, together with density functional theory calculations, reveal that these reconstructed dual-metal interfaces enable cooperative adsorption of NO 3 − and CO 2 , favoring a spatially confined NO─Cu─NO─CO─Bi configuration. This proposed configuration lowers the overall activation barrier and converts the traditionally endergonic C─N coupling into an exergonic N─C─N coupling process, thereby redirecting the reaction pathway toward urea formation while suppressing nitrite and CO byproducts. As a result, the catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 32.7% at −0.4 V vs. RHE with a high yield rate of 2955.3 mg h −1 g −1 at −0.6 V vs. RHE under large current densities. This work provides insights into a generalizable interfacial-site design for modulating reaction pathways in electrosynthetic C─N coupling systems.

10.1002/aenm.71692.abstract: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical reduction of nitrate to ammonia (PEC NO 3 RR) offers a solar‐driven route to NH 3 synthesis under ambient conditions, converting an environmental pollutant into a value‐added product. However, the overall performance of a PEC photoelectrode has been largely governed by the cocatalyst deposited on the light absorber since NO 3 RR conversion is kinetically demanding. Electrochemical NO 3 RR research has produced an extensive library of high‐performance catalysts together with a mature mechanistic understanding. Yet this knowledge has rarely been translated into photoelectrode design. This review summarizes recent advances in PEC NO 3 RR, spanning light‐absorber engineering, photoelectrode–cocatalyst integration, intrinsic semiconductor catalytic activity, and architectures that decouple light absorption from catalysis. On this basis, we reframe the electrochemical NO 3 RR catalyst library as a design resource for PEC cocatalysts and identify key evaluation criteria, such as catalytic activity, interfacial charge‐transfer, optical shading, and stability under illumination and electrically biased conditions. By bridging the mechanistic maturity of electrochemistry with the energetic advantages of photoelectrochemistry, this review provides a coherent design framework for advancing PEC NH 3 synthesis.

10.1002/anie.1513379.abstract: A Janus CuN 3 –PdS 3 dual-atom catalyst on N/S co-doped carbon (CuPd-SNC) spatially decouples nitrate adsorption/activation from hydrogen supply during electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). The Cu sites activate NO x intermediates, Pd sites provide reactive hydrogen, and N/S bridges mediate *H spillover, enabling 99.58% Faradaic efficiency for ammonia synthesis and stable Zn–nitrate battery operation. ABSTRACT Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) using renewable electricity offers a carbon-free and energy-saving route to remediating nitrate-polluted wastewater while producing ammonia (NH 3 ). However, conventional catalysts for NO 3 RR suffer from strong adsorption of NO x intermediates that hinders further hydrogenation, resulting in diminished selectivity and catalyst deactivation. Here we construct a Janus-type CuN 3 −PdS 3 dual-atom catalyst featuring N/S dual bridging, namely CuPd-SNC, to enable decoupled NO x species adsorption and hydrogen supply for hydrogenation on Cu and Pd sites, respectively. Excitingly, CuPd-SNC delivers a near-unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.58% for NH 3 synthesis and a production rate of 1.34 mmol h −1 cm −2 . When integrated into a Zn–nitrate battery, CuPd-SNC achieves a maximum power density of 13.0 mW cm −2 and demonstrates stable operation for >160 h. In situ spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal the site-specific functionalities of the CuN 3 −PdS 3 Janus configuration, wherein Cu sites markedly enhance the adsorption/activation of NO x − intermediates, Pd sites enable continuous proton supply and reduce the energy barriers for multi-step *NO x hydrogenation, while N/S dual bridges serve as a proton reservoir. These findings highlight the site-specific but complementary functioning of dual-atom catalysts in synergistically pushing the limit of conventional electrocatalysts, offering fundamental insights into the rational catalyst design for NH 3 synthesis.

Operando studies provide insight into the function of the promoter. Dynamic surface reconstruction under operating conditions increases the interface between SrO and Co and prevents the blocking of active Co sites by mobile La-containing species. ABSTRACT Storing energy in molecular form, particularly hydrogen in carbon-free carriers such as ammonia, is considered a key strategy for future energy systems. The release of hydrogen via ammonia decomposition is a critical step in this context that requires scalable and economically viable catalysts. In this work, spray-flame synthesis (SFS) was employed to prepare La 1– x Sr x CoO 3− δ (0≤ x ≤ 1) nanoparticles (≈ 10 nm), which serve as precursors for SrO-promoted Co/La 2 O 3 catalysts prepared by exsolution. ESR, operando XRD, and ambient pressure photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provide insights into dynamic interfacial restructuring of the catalysts under the harsh ammonia decomposition conditions. The catalysts contain 25 wt% Co and achieve a maximum hydrogen productivity of 108 mmolH2${\mathrm{mmo}}{{\mathrm{l}}_{{{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathrm{2}}}}}$·g Co −1 ·min −1 at 500°C for the La 0.75 Sr 0.25 CoO 3− δ -derived material. The coverage of La 2 O 3 with SrO/Sr─OH species under reaction conditions inhibits the migration of La-based species, which block active Co sites in the absence of the promoter. An excess of Sr, however, promotes the growth of Co particles and reduces the exposed Co surface area. Beyond its structural role, operando APXPS reveals that SrO also influences reaction kinetics by facilitating NH x decomposition and weakening the binding strength of nitrogen, which is consistent with an electrostatic effect of SrO.

10.1002/anie.3154221.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (eNO 3 RR) offers a sustainable route for nitrate removal and nitrogen valorization, yet its selectivity is governed by complex intermediate evolution. This Review focuses on intermediate behaviors in eNO 3 RR, covering their transformation pathways, detection methods, and regulation strategies. By linking mechanistic insights with catalyst and interfacial design, it highlights opportunities to steer nitrate conversion toward NH 3 , N 2 , or NH 2 OH. ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction reaction (eNO 3 RR) has emerged as a promising strategy for waste NO 3 − valorization, offering opportunities for environmental remediation. However, its complex proton-coupled electron transfer processes involve multiple competing pathways, in which the fate of key intermediates governs reaction activity and product selectivity. In this review, we provide an intermediate-centered perspective on eNO 3 RR, covering the reaction pathways from NO 3 − activation to the selective synthesis of NH 3 , N 2 , and NH 2 OH. We then summarize current techniques for probing N-containing intermediates and active hydrogen (*H). On this basis, we discuss how catalyst design and microenvironment engineering regulate key processes in eNO 3 RR, including intermediate adsorption, retention and desorption, N─O bond cleavage, hydrogenation, and N─N coupling. We also examine the emerging role of data-driven approaches in optimizing eNO 3 RR systems. Drawing these discussions together, we distill principles for selective product synthesis. Finally, we discuss remaining challenges in achieving a deeper mechanistic understanding, regulating the interfacial microenvironment, and applying eNO 3 RR to real wastewater.

Here we introduce a reactant‐shunting strategy that installs a guiding electrocatalytic step via isolated Ru atoms to supply surface‐bound * H species and enforce a Langmuir–Hinshelwood (LH) hydrogenation pathway. Using Ru 1 /Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst, we show that single Ru sites promote water adsorption and dissociation, forming stable Ru‐H intermediates that thermodynamically and kinetically accelerate the coupling‐hydrogenation steps in NORR. The reactant‐shunting principle further generalizes across multiple oxide hosts, enhancing NH 3 productivity by up to threefold. These findings establish pathway steering through controlled hydrogen delivery as a powerful strategy for high‐efficiency electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis.

10.1002/anie.3649572.abstract: We demonstrate that a dynamic asymmetry in the O/N-coordinated Zn single-atom catalysts promotes Sabatier-favorable urea and H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis, enabling subsequent urea peroxide production. ABSTRACT Precise regulation of metal‒intermediate binding is essential for selective electrocatalysis, yet conventional symmetric single-atom coordination often limits directional adsorption control. Here we report an asymmetric O/N-co-coordinated Zn single-atom catalyst, Zn-O 3 N 1 -C, using symmetric Zn-O 4 -C as a structural counterpart. Structural characterization and x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirm atomically dispersed Zn‒O 3 N 1 sites, in which replacing one O ligand with less electronegative N not only breaks local symmetry, but also enriches Zn electron density and lowers the Zn oxidation state. Operando XAS further reveals that Zn–O 3 N 1 undergoes cathodic-bias-induced electronic enrichment and anisotropic Zn─N/Zn─O bond response, amplifying local coordination polarization while preserving the isolated Zn─O/N framework. This dynamically polarized asymmetric coordination shifts Zn‒adsorbate interactions toward a Sabatier-favorable regime, enabling two adsorption-governed transformations. For CO 2 /nitrate co-reduction, Zn-O 3 N 1 -C promotes *NO/*NHO-mediated C‒N coupling. The same catalyst also demonstrates excellent electrocatalytic activity toward two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR). The electrosynthesized urea and H 2 O 2 are further coupled to produce urea peroxide. Operando spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that asymmetric Zn–O 3 N 1 coordination optimizes *NO/*NHO and *OOH binding, establishing dynamic coordination polarization as a design principle for selective single-atom electrocatalysis.

10.1002/anie.3793785.abstract: We have developed a series of Cu 1 /M 1 -NOC dual-atom electrocatalysts for electrochemical urea synthesis via CO 2 and NO 3 − /NO 2 − co-reduction. The modulation of metal sites switches *CO adsorption configuration from bridge-bound to linear-bound (*CO L ), and the electrophilic *CO L greatly facilitates coupling with N-intermediates beneficial for C─N formation. The optimal Cu 1 /M 1 -NOC achieves 73.73% and 67.3% urea Faradaic efficiency with NO 2 − and NO 3 − , respectively. ABSTRACT Electrochemical urea synthesis through CO 2 and nitrate/nitrite (NO 3 − /NO 2 − ) co-reduction represents a revolutionary alternative pathway for urea formation. Although studies reveal that restraining C-intermediates desorption is beneficial for C-N coupling, *CO adsorption behaviors were usually described by *CO binding energy based on DFT calculations. The intrinsic reason why the *CO adsorption behaviors could modulate the activity for urea formation remains ambiguous. Herein, a series of high-density Cu 1 /M 1 -NOC electrocatalysts regarding single-atomically dispersed Cu 1 /Cu 1 , Cu 1 /Ni 1 , Cu 1 /Au 1 , or Cu 1 /Pd 1 sites anchored on N, O-co-doped carbon were developed for electrochemical urea synthesis. In situ spectroscopy reveals that strengthening *CO binding energy not only enhances *CO coverage but also increases the proportion of linear *CO absorption configuration (*CO L ). The *CO L with sp hybridization exhibits stronger electrophilicity than that for bridge adsorption, thereby favoring coupling with N-intermediates. Notably, a linear relationship was established by plotting urea yield versus *CO L coverage. As such, the intrinsic reason for facilitating C─N coupling was originated from the local enrichment of *CO L . The optimal Cu 1 /Pd 1 -NOC catalyst exhibits the high urea Faradaic efficiencies of 73.73% and 67.3% with NO 2 − and NO 3 − as N source, respectively. This research provides an effective strategy to boost urea performance by precisely controlling the *CO adsorption behaviors.

10.1002/anie.7739547.abstract: Hard Lewis acid Mo 6+ induces N-end adsorption of urea to steer selective nitrite electrosynthesis. Directional electron redistribution generates a polarized surface that stabilizes configuration-selective adsorption, promotes C─N bond cleavage, and suppresses competing pathways, enabling efficient nitrogen upgrading from wastewater. ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic urea oxidation reaction (UOR) offers a promising route for coupling wastewater remediation with nitrogen upgrading. However, the structural complexity of urea, containing both electron-donating (─NH 2 ) and electron-withdrawing (C = O) groups, leads to multiple adsorption configurations, resulting in poorly defined pathways and low selectivity toward nitrite (NO 2 ‾ ). Here, guided by Pearson's hard-soft acid-base theory, we develop a hard Lewis acid strategy by incorporating Mo 6+ into NiCo layered double hydroxide (NiCoMo-LDH) to regulate interfacial electronic structure. The strong electron-accepting nature of Mo 6+ regulates the electronic environment of Ni/Co centers, facilitating the formation and stabilization of high-valent NiOOH/CoOOH species while creating polarized interfacial sites with enhanced affinity toward urea activation. Importantly, Mo-induced modulation does not merely increase oxidative capability; instead, it introduces substrate-specific adsorption regulation that favors UOR over the competing OER. This configuration regulation facilitates selective C-N bond cleavage of the *NCONH 2 intermediate and subsequent oxidation of the generated nitrogen species toward NO 2 ‾ , achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 93.4% and a production rate of 1732.7 µmol h −1 cm −2 . This work establishes Lewis acid modulation as a strategy for controlling adsorption configurations and steering selective electrosynthesis.

10.1002/anie.8178911.abstract: CO 2 is not merely a mineralization product: at reduced quinone sites, it forms carbonate adducts that poison 2e − oxygen reduction. A redox-gated pulsed electrocatalysis strategy periodically reoxidizes quinone sites to release bound CO 2 in situ, boosting degradation kinetics and sustaining metal-free electrocatalytic water purification. ABSTRACT Quinone-based metal-free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization-derived CO 2 as the major cause of a previously overlooked self-poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO 2 accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two-electron oxygen reduction to H 2 O 2 and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen-reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO 2 adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential-dependent carbonate-bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO 2 poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox-gated CO 2 switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO 2 -induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO 2 buildup, including CO 2 electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

Their convergence and subsequent coupling through a *NOCO intermediate direct selective formamide formation, establishing a general design principle for electrocatalytic C─N bond construction. ABSTRACT Electrochemical C─N coupling from carbon dioxide and nitrogen oxoanions offers a sustainable route to value-added amides, yet achieving high selectivity remains challenging due to competing reaction pathways and insufficient substrate activation. Here we report a homo/heterogeneous dual-active-center catalyst that integrates molecular copper phthalocyanine with atomically dispersed chromium sites on porous carbon nanospheres to enable selective electrosynthesis of formamide under neutral conditions. The molecular Cu centers selectively reduce CO 2 to CO, while Cr single atoms promote nitrate (NO 3 − ) and nitrite (NO 2 − ) activation to *NO intermediates, furnishing spatially separated yet kinetically matched reactive species. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal *NO─CO coupling via a *NOCO intermediate as the key pathway. This work establishes a general strategy for designing dual-site electrocatalysts for selective C─N bond formation.

10.1002/anie.9199303.abstract: A well-defined stable thiolate-bridged diiron μ -NH complex can serve as a key junction in the bidirectional interconversion between Fe−NH x ( x = 0−2) species, linking the late stage of nitrogen fixation with the early stage of ammonia oxidation. ABSTRACT Iron parent imides serve as key intermediates for iron-promoted nitrogen fixation and ammonia oxidation. However, these active species are difficult to be isolated, and their reactivities are underexplored. So far, only a few multinuclear iron parent imides were reported, but none plays a key intersection during the bidirectional transformation. Herein, we adopt the bulky 1,2,4-tri( tert -butyl)cyclopentadienyl (Cp′) and bidentate 1,3-propanedithiolate (pdt) ligand to provide the steric protection for the reactive [Fe 2 S 2 ] scaffold. As predicted, the highly active imido species can be captured by this [Fe 2 S 2 ] platform to generate a novel thiolate-bridged diiron parent μ -imide complex 3 . Mössbauer spectroscopy and DFT calculation reveal that 3 features a bent {Fe III −NH 2− −Fe III } framework with two anti-ferromagnetic coupled, low-spin Fe(III) centers. Importantly, imide 3 can not only undergo protonation to generate amide and finally release ammonia, but also go through hydrogen atom transfer to regenerate nitride. This reactivity indicates that 3 is a key junction that associates the late stage (N 3− → NH 2− → NH 2 − → NH 3 ) of nitrogen fixation and the initial period (NH 2 − → NH 2− → N 3− ) of ammonia oxidation. Overall, this work provides one available strategy that can stabilize a high-activity imide and investigate its reactivity of bidirectional interconversion.

10.1002/cctc.71109.abstract: ABSTRACT Global ammonia production is dominated by the energy‐intensive Haber‐Bosch process, motivating the development of sustainable electrochemical alternatives. While lithium‐ and calcium‐mediated systems in organic solvents have relatively high yields, aqueous electrochemical nitrogen reduction (N 2 ER) remains inefficient. Density functional theory (DFT) studies have significantly advanced the understanding of N 2 ER in aqueous solution; however, most have focused on thermodynamic and/or kinetic analyses to elucidate reaction mechanisms, while orbital‐level insights remain largely unexplored. Here, we combine DFT calculations with intrinsic bond orbital analysis to examine orbital evolution during 13 protonation steps of N 2 ER. This approach identifies the orbitals responsible for proton accommodation in each intermediate. We find that nine of the 13 steps involve nitrogen lone‐pair orbitals. These results suggest that protonation kinetics in aqueous N 2 ER are strongly influenced by interactions between nitrogen lone pairs and the local solvation environment, including cations and hydrogen bonding. Moreover, surface modifications, which profoundly affect the reactivity of the metal–nitrogen σ bond but have a lesser influence on nitrogen lone‐pair orbitals are not expected to have a direct impact on the protonation kinetics of N 2 ER. Thus, rational manipulation of the local electrochemical environment, rather than solely modifying the catalyst surface, may be essential for improving N 2 ER performance.

10.1002/celc.70324.abstract: Electrochemical palladium membrane reactors traditionally rely on direct cathodic polarization of the palladium membrane to drive hydrogen permeation. This work introduces the wireless electrochemical palladium membrane reactor (wPMR), a design that utilizes bipolar electrochemistry to actuate hydrogen transport without direct electrical connections to the membrane. By redefining the palladium membrane as an “ajar” bipolar electrode, we demonstrate that it functions similarly to a diode, requiring a voltage threshold to initiate selective hydrogen transport along an induced external electric field. As a proof‐of‐concept, we integrated the wPMR with lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction, successfully synthesizing ammonia using hydrogen atoms derived directly from water. Unlike conventional systems that suffer from structural deformation due to lattice expansion, the wPMR maintains membrane integrity by avoiding the lattice‐expanded β‐PdH. Through isotope labeling and operando monitoring, we confirm the synchronous operation of four Faradaic reactions within this reaction geometry. The wPMR thus emerges as a high‐voltage electrosynthetic platform capable of directly delivering hydrogen from water to organic reactions.

10.1002/celc.70328.abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) has emerged as a powerful fabrication strategy for the design of advanced electrocatalysts for water electrolysis. Owing to its sequential self‐limiting surface reactions, ALD enables atomic‐scale control over film thickness, composition, morphology, and interface structure, while simultaneously providing highly conformal coatings on complex and porous substrates. These characteristics make ALD particularly attractive for engineering electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER), where catalyst utilization, stability, and interface properties critically influence electrochemical performance. Beyond catalyst synthesis, ALD has also emerged as a powerful platform for disentangling structure‐activity‐stability relationships in electrocatalysis. This review discusses recent advances in ALD‐enabled electrocatalyst fabrication for water electrolysis, with emphasis on noble‐metal and earth‐abundant catalyst systems, including transition‐metal oxides, sulfides, and phosphides. Attention is given to the role of ALD in controlling catalyst dispersion, stabilizing active phases, tuning oxidation states, and engineering catalyst–support interactions. In addition, recent developments in interface engineering, ultrathin overlayers, and phase‐controlled oxide systems are highlighted. Finally, current limitations associated with scalability, throughput, and processing cost are discussed together with future perspectives involving spatial ALD (SALD), plasma‐enhanced ALD (PEALD), and operando characterization approaches for next‐generation water electrolysis technologies.

10.1002/cnl2.70210.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (eNRR) is considered a promising approach to sustainable ammonia production compared with the Haber–Bosch process. However, eNRR remains significantly hindered by the extreme stability of the N≡N bond, slow proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET), and the kinetically favored hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which collectively reduce ammonia yield and Faradaic efficiency. MXenes represent a unique class of 2D transition‐metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides, distinguished by chemically versatile transition‐metal active sites, defect‐rich structures, tunable surface terminations, and metallic conductivity. These properties enable unprecedented tuning of N 2 adsorption, interfacial charge redistribution, orbital hybridization, and adsorption energetics, enabling selective N 2 activation while minimizing competing proton reduction. This review provides a critical overview of the design principles of MXene‐based electrocatalysts for selective ammonia synthesis. The distinctive contribution of this review is to systematically link MXene composition, vacancy engineering, heteroatom doping, single‐atom anchoring, and assembling MXene heterostructures to their effects on electronic structure, adsorption free‐energy landscapes, NRR pathways, and HER suppression. Particular emphasis is placed on understanding catalytic selectivity in terms of the underlying mechanism and structure–activity relationships, derived through advanced operando characterization, density functional theory, and emerging machine‐learning‐assisted catalyst discovery.

10.1002/cphc.70594.abstract: Uranium nitrides UN 2− x are excellent candidates as catalyst for ammonia synthesis, as demonstrated by their historical precedent. However, despite their potential, uranium nitrides have not been extensively investigated. In this study, we theoretically investigated the bulk and surface properties of pure and defective UN 2 (UN 1.75 ) implementing DFT + U approach. Uranium nitride UN 2 is not stable, and vacancies are spontaneously formed leading to N/U ratio between 1.7 and 1.8 depending on the synthesis conditions. The vacancy formation energy of UN 2 was calculated as −0.70 eV. To identify the most stable surface, surface energy was calculated for both UN 2 and UN 1.75 catalyst built in four Miller indices (100), (110), (111), and (121). It was found that (111) surface is the most stable one. Moreover, considering differences in distribution of vacancies in UN 1.75 , a random vacancy distribution for (111) surface shows the lower surface energy of 0.51 J.m −2 . The surface can easily be covered by layer of oxygen at very low oxygen pressure even at high temperature of 1500 K. However, the regeneration of the initial deoxygenated surface is possible under reaction conditions, (N 2 /H 2 ; 1:3) at 1000 K temperature. Regeneration is further facilitated in the presence of ammonia in the gas mixture.

10.1002/cssc.71148.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia provides a promising strategy for coupling nitrate‐polluted wastewater remediation with distributed ammonia production, but achieving high performance with reasonable selectivity and stability remains challenging. Structural and surface analyses reveal that W incorporation modifies the diffraction features, particle‐stacking morphology, and core‐level electronic states of the NiFeCoRu matrix, indicating local structural distortion and multimetallic electronic coupling rather than simple compositional addition. Benefiting from the W‐containing multimetallic environment and increased electrochemically accessible sites, NiFeCoRuW achieves an NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 98.1% and an NH 3 yield rate of 162.65 mg h −1 mg_cat −1 at −0.5 V versus RHE, outperforming reported high‐entropy‐alloy‐based NO 3 RR catalysts. UV–vis colorimetry and NMR cross‐validation support reliable ammonia quantification. In situ DEMS trends and auxiliary free‐energy profiles further suggest that W‐assisted electronic reconstruction favors nitrate activation and promotes deep reduction involving *NOH/*N‐related intermediates while limiting excessive hydrogen‐evolution competition.

10.1002/ejic.70337.abstract: Excess nitrate (NO 3 − ) and nitrite (NO 2 − ) from agricultural and industrial sources are major water pollutants and precursors of greenhouse gases. The electrocatalytic reduction of NO 3 − /NO 2 − is regarded as a sustainable solution for the remediation of contaminated water and a method for producing ammonia (NH 3 ) under ambient conditions. In this review, molecular electrocatalyst macrocycles derived from heme, such as porphyrins and phthalocyanines, and nonheme complexes for NO 3 − /NO 2 − reduction are presented. Based on enzymes such as molybdenum‐dependent nitrate reductases and copper‐ or heme‐containing nitrite reductases, representative synthetic enzymes are discussed in terms of their mechanisms, catalytic parameters, ligand effects, product selectivity, and stability. The conversion of NO 2 − to NH 3 is the most prominent application of heme‐type Fe and Co macrocycles Nonheme systems, such as Cu polypyridines, Ni diamine, or Fe/Co N‐donor complexes, can also produce NO, N 2 O, or NH 3 by varying the ligand environment or pH. We identified some advances, such as high turnover frequencies, elucidation of the competitive proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and atom transfer pathways, and new strategies for increased durability. Finally, the principles of second‐sphere proton relay and electronic tuning are discussed, and the opportunities for embedding macrocycles within conductive frameworks and emulating multisite enzymatic architectures to create efficient and robust electrocatalysts for nitrogen oxide (NO x ) remediation and green NH 3 production are outlined.

10.1002/open.70305.abstract: This review takes a structure mechanism perspective on active site dynamics and charge transfer pathways governing ammonia selectivity in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). This review aims to summarize the progress of MOF‐based electrocatalysts for nitrate to ammonia conversion, with a focus on structural characteristics, charge transfer behavior, and catalytic activity. The basic principles of nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 − RR) such as reaction thermodynamics, reduction process, and important activity descriptors are presented. The recent developments on pristine MOFs, conductive MOFs, MOF‐derived materials and hybrid architectures are summarized and the roles of metal centers, ligand functionalization, defect engineering, heterometallic interactions and interfacial coupling in controlling nitrate adsorption, intermediate stabilization and hydrogenation processes in MOFs are highlighted. Representative MOF based systems achieve NH 3 Faradaic efficiencies (FEs) up to about 99% with production rates near 22.5 mg h −1 cm −2 and nitrate conversion approaching 99%. The contribution of theoretical calculations and operando characterization techniques toward understanding reaction mechanisms is discussed. Key bottlenecks include low‐intrinsic conductivity, limited structural stability under reducing conditions, uncertain identification of the true active phase during reconstruction, and inconsistent testing protocols across studies. Finally, the current limitations and future research directions for developing stable, conductive, and practically relevant MOF‐based NO 3 − RR catalysts are critically evaluated.

10.1002/smll.76107.abstract: ABSTRACT The large‐scale deployment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells is hindered by the intrinsic activity‐stability trade‐off in Pt‐based alloy catalysts, arising from transition metal dissolution and nanoparticle aggregation. Herein, we develop a mesh‐island confinement strategy to construct a ternary PtCoSn catalyst via alternating atomic layer deposition. In this design, Co preferentially occupies low‐coordination Pt sites, while Sn is selectively enriched on the nanoparticle surface and carbon support. Upon reduction, a PtCoSn alloy core is formed and stabilized by a surface SnO‐based mesh and support‐confined islands. The membrane electrode assembly achieves a peak power density of 1.46 W cm −2 and a mass activity of 0.73 A mg Pt −1 , with only 14.4% performance degradation after 30 000 accelerated durability cycles. This work establishes a general strategy for the rational construction of highly durable electrocatalysts through mesh‐island confinement.

In this study, a visible‐light‐responsive ZnCdS solid solution with engineered sulfur vacancies (ZCS v ) is developed for the efficient synthesis of amides from alcohols and NH 3 . The optimized ZCS v ‐5 catalyst achieves a high formamide yield rate of ∼4.27 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with 87.4% selectivity from CH 3 OH and NH 3 . Projected density of states (PDOS) analysis and in situ X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) provide direct evidence that S v creates a polarized surface environment and Zn sites serve as hole reservoirs, which synergistically facilitate charge separation. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), combined with theoretical simulations, reveal that the exposed Zn sites strengthen reactant adsorption and enable selective activation of C─H and N─H bonds for C─N coupling. Herein, a tandem catalysis strategy is adopted to fabricate a cobalt(III) oxide‐Cu heterostructure on nickel foam (Co 2 O 3 ‐Cu/NF) to enhance NO 3 − RR activity. Coordination distortion and asymmetry confirm the distinctive amorphous nature of Co 2 O 3 . This work overcomes the inherent limitations of Cu‐based catalysts through crystalline‐amorphous dual‐site tandem synergy, offering new insights for developing NO 3 − RR technology.

10.1002/sus2.70103.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven photocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (p‐NRR) offers a sustainable pathway for ammonia synthesis under ambient conditions. However, its efficiency is fundamentally hampered by the kinetic inertness of the N≡N triple bond. Herein, we construct oxygen‐vacancy‐induced asymmetric Co 2+ –Ov–Co 3+ units within two‐dimensional (2D) ultrathin LaCoO 3− x nanosheets to address this challenge. Oxygen‐vacancy‐induced symmetry breaking reconstructs the Co–O coordination field, forming Co 2+ sites with redistributed 3d energy levels that strongly couple with π* orbitals of N 2 . In situ spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations reveal that these asymmetric sites promote directional electron injection, stabilize the key *NNH intermediate, and decrease the transition‐state energy barrier of the rate‐determining step from 1.98 to 1.38 eV. Consequently, the optimized LaCoO 3− x exhibits a photocatalytic NH 3 production rate of 462.6 µg g −1 h −1 , which is 7.7 times higher than that of pristine LaCoO 3 . This work provides a fundamental insight into orbital‐level catalyst design for highly efficient p‐NRR.

10.1007/s10163-026-02749-3.abstract: Abstract Excess nitrogen in high-strength wastewater represents an environmental burden and an untapped resource for recovery. Conventional nitrogen recovery processes, including ammonia stripping, anammox, and struvite precipitation, require ammonium-rich streams. This study evaluates the potential of an anaerobic membrane bioreactor (AnMBR) as a platform for wastewater treatment, energy recovery, and retention of ammonium (NH 4 ⁺–N) in the permeate. A 340-d trial was conducted with synthetic wastewater across six sequential operating periods with hydraulic retention times (HRTs) of 3–5 d and influent ammonium concentrations of 1170–2800 mg NH 4 ⁺–N L⁻¹. Under the baseline condition (5-d HRT; 1170 mg NH 4 ⁺–N L⁻¹), the reactor achieved 98% COD removal, 90% ammonium retention, and methane production of 0.28 L CH 4 g COD⁻¹ d⁻¹. At a 3-d HRT or at higher influent ammonium concentrations, process stability declined, with lower COD removal and ammonium retention accompanied by volatile fatty acid accumulation. Descriptive microbial profiles showed enrichment of stress-tolerant taxa and a shift from acetoclastic to hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis. The principal contribution is therefore the long-term operational evidence that an AnMBR can produce an ammonium-rich, solids-free permeate that may serve as a feed for downstream nitrogen-recovery processes, while defining the operational conditions associated with stable performance.

10.1007/s11085-026-10466-3.abstract: Reliable structural materials are essential for the safety of high-temperature ammonia decomposition systems, where components may experience complex NH3/H2/N2 atmospheres and associated nitridation-induced degradation. This review critically evaluates the high-temperature nitridation and associated degradation mechanisms of austenitic stainless steels and Ni-based alloys exposed to ammonia-containing environments relevant to ammonia decomposition systems. The available literature is analyzed by distinguishing direct ammonia-containing evidence from mechanistic evidence obtained under non-ammonia nitriding conditions, thereby clarifying the applicability and limitations of each evidence base. The review establishes the relationships among nitrogen supply, nitrogen ingress, nitride formation, elemental redistribution, defect evolution, and material degradation. The results demonstrate that nitridation responses are governed by the coupled effects of gas chemistry, temperature, exposure history, alloy chemistry, surface-scale stability, and defect-assisted transport rather than by alloy category alone. Austenitic stainless steels generally exhibit nitrogen enrichment, expanded-austenite evolution, and Cr-rich nitride precipitation, whereas Ni-based alloys tend to develop internal nitridation associated with strong nitride-forming elements such as Cr, Al, Ti, and Nb. These behaviors represent condition-dependent tendencies rather than strict distinctions between alloy classes. Preliminary NH3 exposure experiments on 310S stainless steel at 500 °C and Inconel 600 at 700 °C, each conducted for 300 h at an initial NH3 pressure of 3 MPa, are included as separate case studies to illustrate nitridation-related responses rather than to rank alloy resistance. This review highlights the need for more controlled NH3/H2/N2 exposure studies and coupled microstructural–mechanical characterization to support material selection for future ammonia decomposition systems.

10.1016/j.apsusc.2026.167348.abstract: Rare-earth ceramics are promising plasma etch-resistant coatings because they form stable fluorides. However, the industry-benchmark Y2O3 is limited by high cost and supply-chain risks. Although La2O3 is a more abundant and cost-effective alternative, its application is restricted by strong hygroscopicity. Upon exposure to air, La2O3 readily reacts with H2O and CO2 to form hydroxide and carbonate species, causing volume expansion and reducing density and structural stability. This paper describes the design and realization of atomic layer deposition (ALD)-grown La2O3-Al2O3 composite ceramic films that achieve etch resistance approaching that of Y2O3 while significantly outperforming Al2O3, together with improved environmental stability. Compared with Al2O3, the enhanced etch resistance of the composite films is associated with preferential removal of Al-containing fluorides, which promotes near-surface La enrichment and the formation of a dense La-rich protective layer that suppresses further erosion. Meanwhile, the incorporation of Al2O3 improves the environmental stability of the films by lowering surface basicity, thereby suppressing adsorption of ambient H2O and CO2. Under CF4/O2/Ar plasma, the composite film with 28 at.% La reduces the etch rate of Al2O3 by over 75% to 0.51 nm/min, approaching pure La2O3 (0.33 nm/min), which outperforms the industrial-benchmark Y2O3 (0.53 nm/min).

10.1016/j.biortech.2026.135109.abstract: The electrochemical ammonia stripping (EAS) exhibits considerable potential for the removal and recovery of ammonia nitrogen from biogas slurry. However, its practical application is constrained by the requirement for sulfuric acid as an absorbent, resulting in the formation of acidic nitrogen fertilizer (NF) that lacks suitability for direct application. A combined process integrating EAS with calcium-based ammonia absorption was proposed to address the above limitation. Both solid and liquid phases were characterized throughout the reaction, providing insight into the reaction progression. Based on the results of single-factor optimization, response surface methodology was employed to further optimize the CO2 concentration, aeration flow rate, current intensity, and temperature, achieving a total ammonia recovery efficiency of 96.1 % and a CaSO4 conversion rate of 20.4 %. Notably, the resulting NF exhibited a pH in the range of 6.5-8.5, making it suitable for direct agricultural use. Furthermore, a germination index of 109 % was achieved with the product diluted to 4 %, confirming the NF is no acute phytotoxicity under the tested conditions. In pot experiments with Chinese cabbage, substituting 75 % of urea with the NF resulted in a dry weight of 2.9 g, representing a 20.9 % increase compared to the non-substitution treatment, and the nitrogen use efficiency improved from 5.1 % to 10.2 %. This study provides a cost-effective and sustainable approach for NF production, contributing to the circular utilization of waste resources.
